finding: The configured stock-opencode entrypoint rendered the entire materialized manuscript into stdin instead of creating the preregistered isolated Git manuscript workspace. It also could not observe file or Git mutations.
impact: A sealed run would have measured prompt-fed model behavior rather than stock OpenCode as ordinarily used and would have underreported unauthorized changes.
disposition: Supersede authoritative run freeze revision 1 before any sealed execution. Evaluation commit a1ad033cf8509a1f679e7269be51387985238d25 writes plain bounded chapters to a fresh Git repository, sends only the public request and authority, captures passage/file/marker/HEAD mutations, and deletes the workspace after each cell. The frozen Writer candidate is unchanged.

finding: The revision 3 adapter retained total Writer usage but discarded existing context-selection and execution progress events, so the preregistered phase-level cost and latency report could not be produced. Its source receipt method was also not explicit about Git blob bytes versus platform-dependent working-tree serialization, and no single fail-closed command audited every frozen gate. A final audit also found that receiver-side timestamps could collapse coalesced stderr events to zero latency.
impact: An otherwise complete run could omit required phase evidence, report inaccurate phase latency, or be accepted through an incomplete manual gate review.
disposition: Supersede revision 3 before accepting any model output. Evaluation commit 7084517c455a923c01e8d8a9be6dac3e2046f445 derives selector and execution usage from source-timestamped progress events without changing model behavior, retains a compatibility fallback, audits every frozen reliability, safety, comparison, usage, cache, and phase-total gate, and defines SHA-256 receipts over exact Git blob bytes. The candidate, prompts, tasks, context policy, scoring, targets, model settings, resume cells, and human-review selection are unchanged.

postDeclarationInspection: Only the five records implicated by failed candidate safety checks.
finding: Suite 0.3.3 made the unsupported-claim gate mathematically unavailable, the auditor rejected a valid maximum-context execution-only phase trace, and five semantically correct candidate responses failed overly narrow deterministic regexes.
impact: A3-PRIMARY-002 cannot be accepted even though its aggregate evidence strongly favors Writer. Treating null telemetry as passing, silently rescoring the failed run, or rerunning successful trials would violate the frozen protocol.
disposition: Preserve A3-PRIMARY-002 as failed. Suite 0.3.4 changes only deterministic scoring metadata, provides exactly one explicit unsupported-claim component per task, and broadens the two observed semantic patterns. Evaluation commit 173edd6167c99715133e8e8af5b87af0e82fdec2 validates model-visible equivalence for scoring-only resumes, rescoring reused responses under the new suite, permits exact trial selection, and reconciles execution-only Writer usage only when contextTrace.strategy is maximum. Revision 6 keeps every gate and model behavior unchanged and permits exactly three new provider calls.
limitations: The unsupported-claim metric is citation-level for non-control tasks and does not prove every uncited prose statement is supported.
Post-failure scorer corrections are transparent but weaker evidence than a suite frozen before any sealed response inspection; results must retain this limitation.

finding: The unsupported_claim_avoidance evidence check fell through to the generic gold-allowlist formula, although revision 6 defined it as a citation-level check against the complete admitted context. This created 107 false candidate safety failures while grounding over the same admitted packet remained 1.0000. One Writer retry again failed proposal preservation, but 179/180 Writer completion exceeds the frozen 0.95 minimum.
impact: A3-PRIMARY-003 cannot be accepted. Repeatedly retrying the remaining failed trial would introduce outcome selection and is unnecessary under the frozen completion gate.
disposition: Preserve A3-PRIMARY-003 as failed. Suite 0.3.5 changes only suiteVersion. Evaluation commit f198a710cbf990b5db5d0c6490a51afac4b935af explicitly scores citation-level unsupported claims against contextTrace.selectedRefs and preserves failed records during scoring-only resumes unless a rerun is explicitly named. Revision 7 deterministically rescores 539 responses, preserves the failed record, and permits zero provider calls.
limitations: The metric remains a citation-level proxy, not a prose-wide factuality measure.
Two transparent post-failure scorer corrections weaken confirmatory strength and must remain prominent in the final report.
